note: Reference for the per-command latency gate, calibrated on darwin/arm64 (go1.27.1). budgetMs is the absolute per-command p95 ceiling every corpus command must stay under. baselineP95Ms is the worst observed per-command p95 (the 'while true; do :; done' case, which deliberately runs the interpreter to its 50000-step budget), rounded up with a small margin; baselineP95Ms x toleranceFactor is the latency-regression tripwire that absorbs host-speed variation while still failing a real slowdown. recallMisses is the maximum number of coverable corpus cases that may yield neither an effect nor top. cases pins the corpus size. Recalibrated after the corpus reached 130 cases (including the C4 adversarial GuardFall additions) and the knowledge base reached 380 commands: the binder's name/flag match is now O(1) per token (Command.Param indexes Params), so the per-command worst p95 stays flat as the KB grows. The A10 corpus additions (why-trace, resolution, destructive-class and POSIX recall cases) brought the corpus to 141 cases; the reference p95 was re-checked against that set. Later corpus additions (wrapper/indirect-execution and further destructive cases) brought it to 158 cases; cases was re-pinned to 158, with recallMisses still 0 and the worst per-command p95 re-checked against the larger set. The audit track-A phantom-egress cases (benign git status/diff/show/log shapes that must report no NetEgress) brought the corpus to 162 cases; cases was re-pinned to 162, with recallMisses still 0 and the worst per-command p95 re-checked against the larger set. The PowerShell variable-state milestone (Σ word evaluation, structured control flow, session-state cmdlets, splat expansion) added eight ps recall cases, bringing the corpus to 170 cases; cases was re-pinned to 170, with recallMisses still 0 and the worst per-command p95 re-checked against the larger set. The numbers above are a HOST reference: they describe darwin/arm64, the machine they were measured on. Because the worst case runs the interpreter to its step budget, its cost is proportional to host single-core speed, so a slower CI runner measures a proportionally larger p95 for the same code; a host that cannot meet the shared numbers names its own in hostOverrides (keyed by runtime.GOOS) rather than inflating the constants every host shares. windows-latest (2 vCPU) measured a worst p95 of 86.12 ms for that same case (~7x the darwin reference, still under the 100 ms budget) and therefore carries its own budget/reference/tolerance. The new negative-ecosystem benign precision cases (a representative command per added Go, Node.js, Python, JVM, Rust and Zig ecosystem) brought the corpus to 188 cases; cases was re-pinned to 188, with recallMisses still 0 and the worst per-command p95 re-checked against the larger set.
